aula.titulo: Review and test of the first block
aula.objetivo: Review pronunciation, articles, the present, the accusative, separable verbs, time and directions, fix the most common English-speaker mistakes, and take the test for the first block.

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you ask yes/no questions and questions with wer, was, wo, woher, wohin, wann and wie, and answer in full sentences.

blocos.contexto: Camila is in the classroom. The teacher is taking attendance. Jonas sits next to her.

linhas.ru: — Aus Brasilien. Ich wohne jetzt in München.
linhas.pt: — From Brazil. Now I live in Munich.
linhas.audio: Aus Brasilien. Ich wohne jetzt in München.

linhas.ru: — Hallo, ich bin Jonas. Wo wohnst du?
linhas.pt: — Hi, I'm Jonas. Where do you live?
linhas.audio: Hallo, ich bin Jonas. Wo wohnst du?

linhas.ru: — Cool! Ich auch. Trinken wir nachher Kaffee?
linhas.pt: — Cool! Me too. Shall we grab a coffee later?
linhas.audio: Cool! Ich auch. Trinken wir nachher Kaffee?

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: there's a second trap. Modern English uses "where" for three ideas. German keeps them apart: STEP 2: wo for staying put, wohin for movement towards, woher for movement from — the old English "where, whither, whence".
blocos.comparacao: English builds questions with "do": "Do you live in Munich?" German has no "do" at all: the verb itself moves to first position — Wohnst du in München? Think of English "Are you…?" or "Can you…?", where the verb already comes first, and do the same with every verb.

blocos.titulo: Everything you already know, in one table
blocos.explicacao: This table sums up lessons 1 to 9, one line per point. Reread one line at a time and say an example of your own out loud. If something feels odd, go back to the lesson shown or open the topic in the Grammar tab.

tabela.regra: ei = "eye", ie = long "ee", sch = "sh", ch = soft "kh" (ich) or throaty (Bach), w = "v", v = "f", z = "ts", s + vowel = "z".
The conjugated verb goes in 2nd position; a yes/no question starts with the verb — never with "do".
ich bin, du bist, er ist...; ich habe, du hast, er hat...
du (one friend), ihr (several friends), Sie (formal, one or several).
der, die, das; every noun capitalized; learn the article with the word.
Five patterns: -e, -(e)n, -er, no ending, -s (often with an umlaut).
ein Tisch, eine Lampe, kein Buch; in the plural, keine.
mein, meine…: they agree with the thing owned.
am Montag, im Mai, der 5. Oktober.
Only the masculine changes: der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen.
du isst, er liest, du nimmst.
ich möchte … + second verb in the infinitive, at the end.
Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.

blocos.enunciado: Introduce yourself out loud in 8 sentences: name, where you're from, age, family, where you live, what you eat, when you get up and how you get to work.
Read the alphabet and the combinations ei, ie, eu, au, sch, ch, sp, st out loud.
